conclusion: Published fly Wwox-loss phenotypes are: viable null (adults scored), radiation sensitivity rescued by fly or human gene (abstract only), suppression of Egr/TNF eye damage and loss of Scrib-clone elimination, day-to-night sleep redistribution in the f04545 hypomorph (males, one control, no rescue), and shorter lifespan with higher sleep pressure after neuronal or glial RNAi (one line); climbing is normal.
label: DATO
what_is_missing: Second allele or second RNAi for sleep; rescue arm for sleep and lifespan; protein level; any neuronal physiology.
next_public_step_or_new_experiment: Reproduce sleep with two independent genotypes before any further work.

conclusion: The Alzheimer amyloid work is a different question: toxicity of a transgenic Abeta42 is worsened by Wwox knockdown, and upregulation (fly or human) helps only with the transgene; none of this is a Wwox-loss phenotype and none is transferred to the loss-of-function model.
label: DATO

next_public_step_or_new_experiment: None needed for transfer; the amyloid claims stay out of the WWOX-DEE model.

conclusion: The first phenotype to verify is a quantifiable behavioural readout that already has data: day-night sleep redistribution (Trikinetics) in a null or in two independent knockdowns with a matched background control. Viability to adulthood is already known and gives no observable.
label: INFERENZA
what_is_missing: Reproduction by a second genotype; males and females; effect of background; whether the change is neuronal (elav) or glial (repo).
next_public_step_or_new_experiment: Genetic design: null/hypomorph and TRiP and KK lines with matched controls, sleep over several days, then rescue.

conclusion: No epileptic phenotype is assumed: no source tested seizure-like behaviour or mechanical-shock sensitivity in Wwox-loss flies, so those are proposals only; finer readouts with source support are lifespan, sleep architecture (episode length, sleep pressure), wing-vein ROS (earlier dossier), stress response (radiation, TNF eye) and startle climbing, which is normal.
label: DATO

next_public_step_or_new_experiment: Add a bang-sensitivity or electroshock test only as a labelled new experiment after the sleep readout is solid.

conclusion: A rescue must reverse the chosen readout with fly Wwox and with human WWOX in the allele background and with neuronal and glial drivers separately, at matched expression, with an empty-vector control; the only hWWOX arm now published is overexpression against amyloid toxicity, and the 2005 rescue is abstract-only.
label: INFERENZA

next_public_step_or_new_experiment: Use null/hypomorph background for rescue; keep the RNAi-based arm for tissue specificity only.

conclusion: Variant comparison is limited: overall identity is about 50 percent (65 percent similarity in the paper); the catalytic Y293 to Y288, P47 to P42 and R54 to R49 are conserved, G372 to S367 is not, and the N-terminal alignment (where Ser14 and Tyr33 lie) is low confidence.
label: INFERENZA
what_is_missing: Multiple alignment with more species; structure; whether a fly residue edit is functionally equal to a human missense change.
next_public_step_or_new_experiment: Test human variants only as hWWOX transgenes in the null background and treat the fly protein as a different molecule.

conclusion: One question the fly could ask and the mouse slice cannot: if a Wwox-loss behavioural readout is reproduced, does it change with Nmdar1 gene dosage (genetic reduction, with APV or MK-801 only as a second arm), tested as epistasis in a Wwox null versus control?
label: IPOTESI
what_is_missing: The Wwox phenotype itself (FE06); a baseline sleep effect of Nmdar1 knockdown (it lowers sleep); the single effective MK-801 amount was lethal to some flies.
next_public_step_or_new_experiment: Only after FE06 and FE08; design as a two-by-two genotype table with sleep as readout; no human implication.

conclusion: The fly cannot discriminate: AMPA from kainate at central synapses (the larval NMJ is non-NMDA and cannot test NMDAR dependence), GluN2A from GluN2B (one NR2 only), cortical burst firing, or a drug effect on a human variant. The mitochondrial or hypoxia axis is a separate genetic-interaction question (abstract level) and is not chosen here.
